JUDGMENT

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63720131/
1 accident.
FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL:
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 23.9.2018 at about 6.20 a.m. the petitioner and other passengers were travelling towards Bengaluru from Kunigal in KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-19-F-3001.

entities.text: Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
When the said bus had reached near Ambedkar Nagar, Soluru Hobli, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagara District, at that time, the driver of the said bus, drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side electric pole and capsized the bus on the road side without control over the bus and caused the accident.
As a result of the said accident, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Nelamangala Government Hospital and then shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.

The petitioner has incurred expenses to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 48 years.
He was providing woolen rugs, bedsheet to Kunigal Areas and was earning a sum of Rs.2,000/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not in a position to continue his work.
As such he has lost his earnings.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F- 3001.
In this regard, case has been registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Kuduru Traffic police as per Crime No.255/2018.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner had filed this claim petition, against the respondent, for compensation.
6. After registration of the case, as usual notice was issued to the respondent.

In response to the notice, the respondent has made his appearance through its counsel and filed the written statement,
in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. In the written statement of the respondent, has not seriously disputed the accident, and the injuries, sustained by the petitioner in the accident.
But, denied the allegation of the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is the main contention of the respondent that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Further contended that, on the date of accident, the left front side tyre was burst, consequently, due to break failure, said bus was capsized.
Further, contended that, the respondent had paid interim compensation of Rs.45,000/- to the petitioner.
Further, contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, abnormal and unreasonable.

Apart from this, had Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63720131/
2 denied all other allegations made in the petition in toto.

entities.text: Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With all these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case,
following issues were framed:
*ISSUES*
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 23.9.2018 at about 6.20 a.m. near Ambedkar Nagar, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara District due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-19-F- 3001 ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What order or award?
9.

In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner by name, Ravish B.K., during the course of evidence, placed his affidavit evidence, in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 in the case on hand.

At the time of his evidence, 12 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
10.
On the other hand, to prove the defenses forthcoming in the written statement, the respondent has examined the driver of the KSRTC bus by name Prashantha Reddy as RW1.
At the time of his evidence marked the document as per Ex.R1, for consideration.

11. Heard the argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the respondent.
12.

Consequently, on appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
13.

It is the case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3001, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
On the other hand, the respondent herein, though not seriously disputed the accident, denied the allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
14. On going through the above issue, burden is on the petitioner, to place cogent and convincing evidence on record for consideration.

To discharge the burden lies on the petitioner, relied on his Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63720131/
3 affidavit evidence, wherein, he reiterated the main petition averments with respect to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, as on the date of the accident.
In support of his case and the affidavit evidence he had placed in all 12 documents for consideration to prove the accident, as well as the injuries sustained by him.

In connection with this issue only Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are relevant, herein for discussion, and remaining documents are to be discussed while considering the injuries and the disability of the petitioner with respect to the accident.
15. On the other hand, to prove all the defenses of the respondent, relied on the evidence of its driver by name, Prashantha Reddy, who examined as RW1.
The said witness, in his evidence mainly deposed that, alleged accident was not intentional, due tire burst and break failure, alleged accident had taken place.

But, in support of the said defense and to disprove the police papers, no cogent and convincing documents placed on record, for consideration, except the production of the authorization letter as per Ex.R1.
16.

On going through the material documents placed by the petitioner, as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 speaks that, on the basis of the first information given by the first informant by name Abdul Jabbar, as per Ex.P.2, on the same date of the accident, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

It is pertinent to note that, there is no delay in giving first information about the accident, and the complainant is none other than the passenger of the offending vehicle, as on the date of the accident.
The recitals of the Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, which laid down the foundation to the criminal case, in connection with the alleged accident, remained unshaken.
Either the respondent authority, or the driver of the offending vehicle, was not made an effort to question these two documents, before the competent court of law.

The Ex.P.3, statement of the victim, substantiates the recitals of the Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.
17.
After setting criminal law in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, the investigation officer visited the scene of offence and conducted spot mahazar process as per the Ex.P4.
In the said document, there is a clear narration about the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Another document, Ex.P.5 seizure mahazar gives clear picture about the genuineness of the fact of the involvement of the offending vehicle, in the accident.
Wound certificate placed by the petitioner marked at Ex.P7 reveals that, he had sustained grievous injury in the said accident.

Added to this, as per the report of the motor vehicle inspector marked at Ex.P6, damages found on the vehicle reflects about the rashness and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and the said accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the offending and defending vehicles.
There is no whisper in the said document, about the technical defect or break failure of the offending vehicle, as on the date of the accident.

18. Another material document Ex.P8- Charge sheet and the statement of the witnesses, submitted by the investigation officer discloses that, the investigation officer, after due investigation process,
filed final report indicating that, the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident,
and the said driver by name Prashanth Reddy, is liable for punishment U/s 279, 337, 338 and section 427 of IPC.
In counter to the recitals of the said documents, no contra materials available on record.

No doubt, the police papers are not substantive piece of evidence, but in the absence of the Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63720131/
4 contra materials, the said police papers, mainly the charge sheet can be considered as conclusive proof in connection with the above issue.
19.

entities.text: Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of cross-examination of PW1, though several questions put to this witness, nothing worthwhile has been elicited to disbelieve his assertion against the driver of the offending vehicle.

On the other hand, at the time of the cross examination of the R.W1, admitted that, as on the date of the accident, he was the driver of the offending vehicle, and the said vehicle was in order and also in proper condition, when it was handed over to him.
The said answer clearly evident that, in connection with the defense of the driver of the offending vehicle, no supportive answer or documents is available on record.
Apart from this, it is also to be noted that, final report has been filed against him, in connection with the accident, the same has not been questioned.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, by way of affidavit and the documentary evidence,
speak that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondent has utterly failed to prove its defenses, and to show that, the petitioner had engineered the documentary evidence.

Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory evidence to prove the above issue to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3001.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

22. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

23. In the light of the preposition laid down in the above case, it is also relevant to note that, "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.

That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63720131/
5 in the way of making a correct assessment.

entities.text: Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
24. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, to substantiate his contention that,
he had sustained injury in the accident has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P7.

The said document discloses that, he sustained the following injuries:-
1) Swelling over left side neck tenderness present 2) Tenderness infront of right side lower part of chest 3) Tenderness over right lumbar region 4) Tenderness over right scapular region 5) Tenderness over back of left hip joint 6) Tenderness over left ankle joint 7) Right side 9th rib fracture with soft tissue Diagnosis right side thorax 9th rib fracture 25.
According to the doctor, the injury No.2 is grievous in nature and other injuries are simple in nature.
Apart from this, the petitioner had produced discharge summary, x-ray, medical bills as per Ex.P9 to Ex.P11.

On going through the discharge summary as per Ex.P9, pertaining to the Adichunchanagiri Hospital & Research Centre, Nagamangala Taluk, reveals that, the petitioner was admitted for treatment on 25.9.2018 and discharged on 29.9.2018.

entities.text: Adichunchanagiri Hospital & Research Centre, Nagamangala Taluk
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
For having taken note of the injury sustained by the petitioner & by taking note of the nature of the injuries sustained by him,
and by keeping in mind about his sufferings during the said period of treatment, in connection with the injury, I am of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.
26.
Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
In the petition, he had stated that, he was selling woolen rugs and bed sheets at Kunigal area and getting an income of Rs.2,000/- per day.
But not produced any iota of documents in this regard.
And the injury sustained by him is grievous in nature, as per the wound certificate.

On going through the discharge summary as per Ex.P9, pertaining to the Adichunchanagiri Hospital &
Research Centre, Nagamangala Taluk, reveals that, the petitioner was admitted for treatment on 25.9.2018 and discharged on 29.9.2018 Hence, definitely there was some difficulty to him, during the period of treatment, to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for one month, due to one fracture, which is grevious in nature, and remaining are simple in nature.

entities.text:
Adichunchanagiri Hospital &
Research Centre, Nagamangala Taluk
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Hence,
I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.12,500/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63720131/
6 27.

entities.text: Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence placed 20 medical bills of Rs.3,000/-.

The said documents not seriously disputed by the other side,
except the suggestion that, the said medical bills are created documents.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,000/- under the head of medical expenses.

28. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, had sustained Swelling over left side neck tenderness present, Tenderness infront of right side lower part of chest, Tenderness over right lumbar region, Tenderness over right scapular region, Tenderness over back of left hip joint,
Tenderness over left ankle joint and Right side 9th rib fracture with soft tissue.
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he took the treatment as an inpatient for 5 days at Adichunchanagiri Hospital Balagangadharanatha nagara, Nagamangala Taluk.
He was discharged with advice of follow up treatment and bed rest.
The mode of treatment, his assertions about the treatments, remained unquestioned and unchallenged by the other side.
As such, during the period of treatment, the petitioner could have taken the assistance of the attendant for travelling, and he could have spent some amount towards travelling, food and nourishment.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.

29. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, he sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injury sustained by him, except his evidence and documents through him, has not made an effort to place the evidence of the doctor, to assess the permanent physical disability, and also to assess the loss of future income, as per the Government notification.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitle for the compensation under the head of loss of future Income due to want of evidence on record.

30. Next factual aspect of loss of amenities is concerned, on going through the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, and also as per the evidence of the PW1 and also the documents placed by him as well as the recitals medical records submitted by the petitioner herein, and also, in the light of the entire facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.
20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
31.
In connection with the future medication expenses is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any documents for consideration.
Hence, I am of the view that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of future medication.

32. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in toto, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Pain and Suffering Rs. 60,000-00 2.Loss of income during laid-up Rs. 12,500-00 period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs. 3,000-00 Ravish B.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63720131/
7
4.Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 10,000-00 Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income NIL 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.
Future medication NIL Total Rs.1,05,500-00 33.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,05,500/-(Rupees one lakhs five thousand and five hundred only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

entities.text: Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
34.
As regards the liability is concerned, in the case on hand, accident has not been seriously disputed by the other side.
Further, the evidence given by the petitioner that, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-19-F-3001, remained unquestioned.
As such, the respondent being the owner cum internal insurance company has to pay compensation to the petitioner, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its realization.

Another point to be discussed herein that, since the interium compensation of Rs. 5,000/- given by the respondent, authority, and the same has been admitted by the PW1, at the time of cross examination, is meager, the said ex-gratia amount has not been deducted.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
35.

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

Consequently, the petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.1,05,500/- (Rupees one lakhs five thousand and five hundred only) , along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/-.
